standard.title: Words work together in sentences
standard.description: recognise that sentences are made up of groups of words that work together in particular ways to make meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students recognise that sentences express ideas (AC9EFLA05). They have not yet examined how words within a sentence work as a system — how nouns connect to verbs, or adjectives to nouns.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify that words in a sentence have particular roles and work together — nouns, verbs and adjectives connect to make meaning — and can demonstrate this across multiple simple examples.

nodes.label: Words have jobs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that words in a sentence do different things — some name things, some describe actions, some describe qualities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one noun (a naming word) and one verb (a doing word) in a simple sentence.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise that words play different roles in sentences: nouns name things, verbs describe actions or states, adjectives describe qualities; identify examples in simple sentences.
wider: Sort word cards from familiar sentences into 'naming words', 'doing words' and 'describing words' categories
Identify the same word playing different roles in different sentences — for example, 'run' as a noun vs a verb
nodes.hinge_reason: Without distinguishing word roles (naming, doing, describing), students cannot identify how those words connect and relate to each other in Node 2 — word connection reasoning presupposes that the roles are already distinguished.

response_modes.reason: Students need to encounter many examples of each word class before the categories become robust — a single example of a noun or verb is insufficient. Accumulating examples is the learning work.

success_criteria: Student can point to a noun and a verb in a simple sentence.
Student can say what job each word is doing — naming, doing or describing.

nodes.label: Words connect to each other
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how specific words in a sentence relate to each other — how a noun connects to a verb, or an adjective to a noun.
nodes.minimum_width: Show how a noun and verb connect in one simple sentence (e.g. 'the cat ate').
nodes.typical_width: Identify how words in a sentence relate to one another: how a noun connects to a verb (the subject doing the action), and how an adjective connects to a noun (describing it); apply this to multiple simple sentences.
wider: Use physical sentence-building activities — word cards, sentence strips — to construct and break sentences, discussing which words connect
Explore how changing the connecting word (adjective or verb) changes the meaning of the whole sentence
Identify word connections across a range of text types — picture books, labels, captions — noting how the same patterns appear in different contexts

response_modes.reason: The relationship between words in a sentence is not immediately obvious — students need a visible reasoning scaffold (which word connects to which, and how) before they can apply the pattern independently. Worked examples that make the connection explicit are important here.

success_criteria: Student can identify the noun-verb relationship in a simple sentence.
Student can identify what an adjective is describing in a simple sentence.
Student can explain how removing one word affects the meaning of the sentence as a whole.
